correctness.rationale: The transition P(K_{t+1}=K_t+1 | F_t)=alpha K_t/t is exact for all p,q with p+q=alpha. On the wait-survival event K remains k, yielding the product and gamma ratio. The probability K_n=1 cancels the n-dependent leading gamma coefficient; the disjoint first-success decomposition yields K_n=2 and the second coefficient. For 0<alpha<1, conditional first-class 1/m error is o(m^(-2alpha)), and higher k classes are o(m^(-2alpha)). Tail summation gives the sharp moment cutoff. The joint limit uses the cited, independently established activity limit K_n/n^alpha -> M>0 and a controlled logarithmic expansion with errors O(n^(-alpha)+n^(alpha-1)); classic Mittag-Leffler asymptotics give the macroscopic exponent. Independently checked the first two coefficients for 21 rational finite-n cases. Neither finite arithmetic nor a sampled ML computation proves the cited general a.s. count limit.

value.rationale: Waiting to the next actual move is natural for intermittent full-memory dynamics; a deterministic-time heavy-tail invariant coefficient, the explicit correction, infinite finite-n mean and distinct large-observation-time exponent quantify a genuine aging/order-of-limits phenomenon beyond the already-known activity count law.

final_claim: For full-memory elephant walks with stop probability 0<r<1 and nonzero initial step, the forward wait W_n for the next nonzero increment has exact finite-time conditional gamma-product survival; for every fixed n its far tail has universal coefficient m^(-alpha)/Gamma(1-alpha) plus explicit m^(-2alpha) term and infinite mean; jointly (K_n/n^alpha,W_n/n^(1-alpha)) converges to (M,E/(alpha M)) with Mittag-Leffler M, giving a distinct limiting exponent-one tail.
limitations: Requires uniform full memory, nonzero first move, 0<alpha<1, fixed stop probability and deterministic observation time; excludes partial memory, renewal independence and uniform joint m,n tail asymptotics.
